questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me, it was important to do my exchange in an English-speaking country since I study English, so it made the most sense academically. I ended up choosing Ireland as my exchange destination partly because I had been there once before on holiday, which made it easier to imagine myself living there. The most crucial aspect, however, was that Ireland is part of the EU, which made it possible for me to do my exchange through the Erasmus programme. Ever since I started my studies, I had known that I wanted to go on an Erasmus exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I lived on campus and received my UCARD upon arrival so it really couldn't have been much easier.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to the 24/7 reception desk at the village (student residence) at checked in, got my UCARD and was shown to my room. Super easy and convenient.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation week, which took place the week before the start of the trimester, was very poorly planned and executed. Some events did not take place at all, while others that were scheduled to last two hours were over in just 20 minutes. The one positive thing I can say about the orientation is that the campus tour was well organised. Ironically, the rest of the programme was so poorly executed that it became a bonding experience, as I ended up making friends with other students by sharing our frustration.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were several different residence options available at various price points and with different types of accommodation. The more affordable options were located in slightly older buildings and offered dormitory-style housing, where two students shared a room as well as bathroom facilities with other residents on the same floor. The more expensive options were en-suite rooms in newer buildings, where each student had a private bedroom and bathroom. Regardless of the type of accommodation, all campus residences had shared kitchen facilities.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: One of the student residences included three meals a day, but this was reflected in its already high rental price. The other residences had shared kitchens, and the number of students sharing a kitchen depended on the type of accommodation. In my apartment, four students shared one kitchen, while in other residences, a kitchen could be shared by eight or even more students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: On-campus housing and dorm culture may not be the same at your host institution as they are in your home country. I currently live in a dorm in Copenhagen and really enjoy the strong sense of community it provides. However, this was not my experience at UCD. Although the university had a ResLife app and organised some activities for residents, the overall atmosphere was not as community-oriented as I was used to or had hoped for.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a first come first serve registration, so you had to be quick if you wanted to be sure to get the courses you set yourself up for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: For help we could email the host uni's erasmus coordinators

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful. I had to substitute 2 courses though to make my timetable add up.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have some backup courses as the ones you want may be filled already or there could be some overlap in timetables.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took electives and that included a mix of introductory courses and more advanced courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH all of my courses consisted of a lecture followed by a seminar. At UCD I had some courses that were strictly lectures as well as some strictly seminar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Reading Irish Studies (IRST20060), The British Celts (CCIV10030), Exploring Ireland (IRST30160), Irish Fiction After 2010 (ENG31930) and Children's Literature (ENG10020)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i recommend taking some Ireland centric courses, specifically "Reading Irish Studies" (IRST20060) and "Irish Fiction After 2010" (ENG31930). These are both seminar based courses so you engage a bit more hands on with the materials.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a bunch of different societies and sports clubs at UCD. I joined the Nordic Society and Film Society.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Doing the on campus pub quiz at the clubhouse bar every Tuesday.
Going on hikes outside of Dublin to appreciate the nature.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on daytrips or even weekend trips to other cities around Ireland. I recommend a weekend in Galway.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy to be fair, I don't think there are any major cultural differences.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and societies!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None that I can think of.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture is very nice. Pints and live music, what's not to like?

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Get a student leap card ASAP
2. Join clubs and societies, I regret not joining more
3. Explore Dublin, don't just stay on campus

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Cheap pints at Johnny Rush's. 
For St. Patricks Day don't even attempt to take the bus into town, just walk.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The lifelong friends i made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living on the ground floor.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
